bihar_raw_news.title: Andhra Pradesh Tops First Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index ; Uttar Pradesh Ranks Last
bihar_raw_news.content: Skip to content Dealerships Used Vehicle Sales Andhra Pradesh has topped the first Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI), released by IndiaTech.org in partnership with Consumer VOICE. The index ranks 15 States and Union Territories on how easily a citizen or dealer can buy, sell and transfer a pre-owned vehicle. Andhra Pradesh scored 5.91 out of 10, followed by Kerala at 5.74. Uttar Pradesh came last at 2.47, just behind Bihar at 2.51 and West Bengal at 2.56. No State crossed 6.0. Eight of the 15 states sit in a narrow band between 3.8 and 4.3, which suggests the problems run across the system rather than in a few lagging states. Together, the 15 states account for over 85% of India’s organised used-car market. The EVOI scores each state on six pillars: policy and regulatory framework, digital infrastructure, process efficiency, transparency and accountability, institutional ecosystem and dealer support, and cost and affordability. The pillar scores are combined using a weighted geometric mean, so strength in one area cannot hide weakness in another. The findings draw on a pan-India survey of over 1,000 buyers and sellers, interviews with dealers, RTO agents and sector experts, and a review of central and state motor vehicle rules. Launching the report, the Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Mr. Harsh Malhotra said, “The used car market in India is very big, and many people buy their first car as a second-hand or used car. I remember my first car, which was also a pre-owned car. While there are hassles and challenges in the transfer of ownership, the integration of policies and their implementation across States is very important, as differences in state-level governance often lead to problems. The Central Government is working on policies in this regard, and we are also taking steps such as setting up automated testing stations, which provide considerable relief, promote ease of doing business and help eliminate corruption. There is always scope for improvement, and we will discuss the recommendations basis this report findings to further enable ease of mobility.” Cost emerged as the weakest pillar nationally, with 12 of the 15 States scoring below 3.5. Manual verification and informal payments push the real cost of a transfer to nearly 10 times the statutory fee. In Bihar, a single transfer can cost ₹13,000 to ₹14,000 over and above the fee prescribed on VAHAN. At border RTOs in Tamil Nadu such as Hosur and Krishnagiri, an official fee of about ₹800 becomes ₹7,000 to ₹8,000. Transfer times also vary widely. A typical registration certificate (RC) transfer takes seven to 10 days in Andhra Pradesh, where the buyer, seller and lender authenticate biometrically, but more than 30 days in Uttar Pradesh. In 13 of the 15 States, applicants who file online are still asked to deliver physical copies to the RTO. Road tax on a ₹6 lakh petrol car ranges from 3% in Uttar Pradesh to 14% in Karnataka and Telangana, a difference of over ₹66,000 on the same vehicle.

bihar_raw_news.title: "Did not receive special package for floods;": Tejashwi Yadav targets PM Modi ahead his Bihar visit
bihar_raw_news.content: "Did not receive special package for floods;": Tejashwi Yadav targets PM Modi ahead his Bihar visit ANI | Updated: Nov 06, 2026 01:37 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 6 (ANI): Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Thursday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of his upcoming visit to the state, alleging that Bihar had not received adequate support from the Centre and that the state government had failed to address issues such as crime, education and healthcare. Yadav said the people of Bihar had given the Prime Minister a massive mandate but continued to be treated like "stepchildren" whenever the state needed assistance. "The Prime Minister is coming to Bihar, yet he has failed to fulfil any of the duties expected of a Prime Minister. The people of Bihar gave him a massive mandate, but whenever Bihar is in need, we are treated like stepchildren. We did not receive a special package for the floods; the Bihar government's coffers are empty. Of the 'double-engine' government, one engine is fuelled by corruption, while the other is driven by crime; an atmosphere of anarchy has taken hold in Bihar. Now that he is visiting, he will surely resort to empty rhetoric," he said. Questioning the development record of the state government, the RJD leader said Bihar continued to rank at the bottom across sectors, including education and healthcare, citing NITI Aayog reports. "They (the ruling side) always repeat the same rehearsed lines. How long has Narendra Modi held the office of Prime Minister? His government has been in power here consistently. NITI Aayog reports indicate that we rank at the very bottom across all sectors—from education to healthcare. The situation remains exactly the same today; there has been no improvement whatsoever," Yadav said. He also criticised Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the law-and-order situation in the state, questioning the government's response to incidents of crime across districts. "Is there any district here where crime does not occur? Yet, we have a Chief Minister who seems to think that the terms 'apradh' and crime are different things. One is an English word, and the other is a Hindi word, but the meaning is exactly the same. He is making Bihar a laughing stock. What can one expect from such a Chief Minister? What will become of Bihar?" he said. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push With Monthly Business Meets - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push as CM Orders Monthly Business Meets Breaking News Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push as CM Orders Monthly Business Meets By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed the state industries minister and district authorities to hold regular meetings with entrepreneurs, signalling a faster grievance-redressal approach for businesses operating across the state. The instruction was issued at the 82nd annual function of the Bihar Industries Association (BIA), which the chief minister inaugurated. Choudhary asked Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh to conduct monthly meetings with entrepreneurs and ensure that their suggestions are considered while framing industrial policies. He also urged district magistrates and superintendents of police to organise similar interactions with entrepreneurs in their respective districts. The directions place district-level administration at the centre of Bihar’s effort to address industrial concerns. The proposed meetings are intended to provide a formal channel for businesses to raise issues and seek quicker resolution from officials responsible for local administration, land and law-and-order matters. Speaking at the event, Choudhary said nearly 1,000 industrial units had moved to the implementation stage during the past year. The statement did not provide a district-wise breakdown of these units or specify the investment value and employment potential associated with them. The chief minister also said several long-pending issues connected with Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority land had been resolved. He referred to the introduction of a new land allotment and management policy, but the details of the policy, including its operational provisions and implementation timeline, were not provided in the supplied report. Industrial land administration has been a recurring concern for businesses because the availability, allotment and management of land influence whether proposed projects can move from announcement to implementation. By linking entrepreneur meetings with district officials and the industries department, the government is seeking to create more direct administrative engagement around such concerns. The event also brought a specific policy request from industry representatives. In response to the demand for a dedicated pharmaceutical policy, Choudhary asked entrepreneurs to prepare a draft proposal and submit it to the government for consideration. The next step, therefore, rests with the industry to frame and send the proposal before the state examines it. Singh attended the BIA function as chief guest. The association also presented its 2025-26 memorial awards to Patel Agri Industries, Banke Bihari Foods, Badshah Industries and former BIA president Arun Agrawal for their contributions to the sector. The government’s immediate implementation milestones are the proposed monthly meetings led by the industries minister, similar district-level interactions involving district magistrates and police superintendents, and the submission of the pharmaceutical policy draft by entrepreneurs. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During Modi’s Vaishali Visit Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During Modi’s Vaishali Visit By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to address a public meeting in Vaishali on November 21, where he may formally inaugurate construction work on the Patna-Purnia Expressway, Bihar’s proposed first national expressway. The six-lane greenfield project is planned to connect Vaishali with Purnia through five districts and could become a major addition to the state’s east-west road network. The public meeting will be held at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area in Vaishali district, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi said after a meeting of National Democratic Alliance constituents at the chief minister’s residence. The visit is planned around the completion of one year of the Bihar NDA government’s present term on November 20. Saraogi said the Prime Minister’s visit was expected to bring new projects for Bihar, but the available announcement does not establish that all the proposed projects will receive final approval or inauguration during the event. The Patna-Purnia Expressway is among the projects expected to feature prominently in the programme. The proposed expressway will begin at Mirnagar on NH-22 in Vaishali district and pass through Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura before reaching Chand Bhatti on NH-27 in Purnia. The planned six-lane, greenfield alignment is intended to create a faster road connection across north and eastern Bihar, linking districts that currently depend heavily on existing highways and local road networks. The project’s significance lies in the scale of the proposed corridor and its potential role in connecting urban centres, district headquarters and rural production areas. However, the source report does not provide the expressway’s approved cost, total length, land-acquisition status, construction schedule or traffic projections. Those details will be important in determining how quickly the corridor can move from a political announcement to implementation. Modi may also inaugurate or lay the foundation stones for other projects in Bhagalpur and Banka districts. These could include a proposed central university near Vikramshila and the proposed Ajgaibinath Greenfield Airport near Sultanganj in Bhagalpur district. The report does not specify their project costs, land requirements or expected completion timelines. The Prime Minister’s visit is also being organised against the backdrop of discussions within the NDA following the Janata Dal (United)’s defeat in three of four seats in the October 23 legislative council elections. Saraogi said the alliance meeting focused on preparations for the visit, while JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha said the alliance remained intact and that the relationship between the BJP and JD(U) had endured for two decades. Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) state president Surendra Vivek also said there was no resentment within the alliance. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects Breaking News Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed officials to accelerate the rollout of the Viksit Bharat-Rozgar evam Aajeevika Guarantee Mission-Rural, or VB-G RAM G, with the state targeting 3 lakh projects worth Rs 22,000 crore for rural employment and village development. Chairing a review meeting on Thursday, Choudhary stressed that rural households should receive 125 days of guaranteed employment annually under the mission. He also instructed officials to ensure that wages are paid within 15 days, making timely disbursal a central implementation priority. The number of projects planned under the mission is to be increased from 1.5 lakh to 3 lakh. According to the state government, the programme is intended to support rural employment, strengthen livelihoods and advance infrastructure development across villages. The chief minister identified water security, rural infrastructure, livelihood enhancement and disaster management as the four key intervention areas. The planned works include Anganwadi centres, additional classrooms in schools, healthcare facilities, rural markets and playgrounds. The programme will also cover the renovation of canals, reservoirs and other water bodies. These projects place water management and basic public infrastructure within the same employment and village development framework, according to the details presented at the meeting. The state has set a specific construction and furnishing allocation for Anganwadi centres. Each centre will receive Rs 12 lakh for construction, along with an additional Rs 2 lakh for furnishings, educational materials and furniture. Rural Development Department Additional Chief Secretary H R Srinivas presented the mission’s features, action plan and implementation strategy during the review. The meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Building Construction Department Minister Leshi Singh and senior departmental officials. The scale-up places responsibility on district and local implementation systems to identify works, execute projects and process wage payments within the stated timeline. The government’s emphasis on water bodies, schools, healthcare facilities and village markets also links employment generation with the delivery of community assets. The state government said effective implementation of VB-G RAM G would provide fresh momentum to the comprehensive development of villages. The next stage is the incorporation and execution of the expanded project list under the mission, alongside monitoring of wage payments and the identified priority works. national_raw_news.content: In hockey, it was ‘Chak Dey’ moment for the defending champion India as the team lifted the trophy for the 6th time by defeating Japan 4-1 in the finals of 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali, last evening. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the jubilant crowd and the Nation celebrated the win as a Diwali gift by the hockey boys ahead of the festival. Although this was India’s third successive title, the winning team had to earn it against a strong defence by the rival team. An early lead by the Samurais kept the Indian Tigers on the toes till the end of the 3rd quarter, when they equalised the goal. The fourth and last quarter was dominated by India as the boys striked thrice to take an unassailable lead and won the Gold. India’s title-winning run was a perfect farewell to midfielder Nilakanta Sharma, who played his last international match in the national jersey. In another match for Bronze, Malaysia defeated South Korea by 5-2 . Celebrating India’s title win, Hockey India has announced a cash reward of Rs. 3 lakhs for each player and 1.5 lakhs for each member of the support staff.

national_raw_news.title: Govt building modern sports ecosystem through Khelo India and TOPS, says PM Modi 9 hours ago 448
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the government is building a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots programmes, Khelo India Centres and Olympic-standard training under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). Felicitating India’s Asian Para Games 2026 contingent for its record haul of 114 medals, Prime Minister urged the athletes to build on their success as they prepare for the Los Angeles 2028 Games. Prime Minister also recalled his appeal from the Red Fort encouraging young people to participate in a nationwide talent hunt with the Olympics in focus. He said Para-sports also receive equal priority under these initiatives. Interacting with the contingent at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, PM Modi said the performance reflected India’s emergence as a major global sporting power. He congratulated the athletes, their families, coaches and trainers, saying the players had won both medals and the hearts of millions. India secured 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Comparing the achievement with the country’s tally of 14 medals, including one gold, in 2010, PM Modi credited the athletes’ perseverance and dedication. The Prime Minister noted that 34 of the contingent’s 56 female athletes won medals, while Indian competitors swept all three podium positions in four events. The team also won nine gold medals on the final day. Highlighting individual performances, PM Modi said Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting, while Haney improved his own world record. He also praised Himanshu, Ravi and Jehan for overcoming physical challenges through their performances. Recalling the sacrifices behind sporting success, PM Modi spoke about Rinku, who lost his mother two months before the Games and held up her photograph after winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” he said. The Prime Minister also highlighted the achievements of younger athletes, noting that 36 of the 61 debutants won medals and Sandeep set a world record on his debut. Describing sports as a means of personality development and nation-building, PM Modi said it teaches discipline, teamwork and the ability to recover from setbacks. He added that the expansion of sports infrastructure, equipment manufacturing and broadcasting was creating employment opportunities beyond the playing field.

national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said India expects to exceed its 220 billion dollar investment target for adding 190 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030. Addressing the media at the conclusion of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit 2026, the Union Minister said that investments totalling 7 lakh crore rupees, including domestic funds and foreign direct investment, have flowed into the renewable energy sector over the past two years. Mr Joshi said the momentum would continue and India would meet the 500 GW target on schedule. He added that strategies are also being prepared to add another 300 GW as directed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said that at present, the country’s installed power capacity from non-fossil fuels stands at 310 GW, and the Union government has fixed a target of reaching 500 GW by 2030. Meanwhile, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Secretary, Santosh Kumar Sarangi said the government is preparing new guidelines for recycling solar module waste. The Summit was inaugurated by Prime Minister on 2nd November 2026. In his address, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic importance of India’s sustained investments in renewable energy in strengthening the country’s resilience to global disruptions, arising from COVID-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis. He observed that India’s investment in the renewable energy sector has largely shielded the country from these disruptions.

national_raw_news.title: From snow leopards to coral reefs: India’s biosphere reserves connect conservation with livelihoods
national_raw_news.content: In the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, an invasive shrub is finding a second life as elephant sculptures, furniture and handicrafts. Indigenous artisans use uprooted Lantana vines to create objects that support livelihoods while drawing attention to the damage the plant causes to forests. In 2021, 125 life-sized Lantana elephants were displayed in London, carrying a message of coexistence with wildlife. Similar sculptures have appeared at Bengaluru Airport, across Bengaluru and at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The initiative illustrates the idea at the heart of biosphere reserves: protecting nature while creating opportunities for the people who depend on it. As the International Day for Biosphere Reserves is observed on November 3, India’s network of 18 notified reserves demonstrates how conservation, scientific research and sustainable livelihoods can work together. Thirteen of these reserves belong to UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves, the highest number in South Asia. The landscapes range from the forests of the Western Ghats and the mangroves of the Sundarbans to the coral reefs of the Gulf of Mannar and the high-altitude Cold Desert of Himachal Pradesh. Conservation beyond protected boundaries India is one of the world’s 17 mega-biodiverse countries. Despite occupying only 2.4 per cent of Earth’s land area, it accounts for approximately 7–8 per cent of recorded species worldwide. Protecting this diversity requires attention to habitats, species and genetic variation, alongside the needs of communities that rely on natural resources. Biosphere reserves provide a framework for bringing these objectives together. While national parks and wildlife sanctuaries primarily protect wildlife and habitats under India’s wildlife protection laws, biosphere reserves take a broader approach, connecting protected ecosystems with surrounding settlements and economic activities. UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere Programme, launched in 1971, promotes scientific approaches to improving relationships between people and their environment. Biosphere reserves serve as living laboratories where sustainable development practices can be tested and demonstrated. Their work combines three functions: conserving biodiversity and landscapes, supporting environmentally responsible economic development, and advancing research, monitoring, education and training. Three zones, connected purposes A biosphere reserve’s structure reflects this balance. Its core area provides the highest level of protection, conserving habitats, species and genetic resources. Human activity is strictly limited, with compatible research and monitoring supporting conservation. The surrounding or adjoining buffer zone accommodates activities such as environmental education, scientific research and regulated ecotourism. These help build ecological understanding while reducing pressure on the core. The transition area supports settlements and livelihoods, including responsible agriculture, sustainable forestry and locally appropriate tourism. Globally, core areas account for an average of 18 per cent of biosphere reserves, buffer zones for 30 per cent and transition areas for 52 per cent. The distribution underlines the importance of inhabited, working landscapes within the conservation model. A network spanning India’s ecological diversity Nilgiri, designated in 1986, was India’s first biosphere reserve. It entered UNESCO’s World Network in 2000. Spread across 5,520 square kilometres in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, the reserve includes tropical evergreen forests, montane shola forests and grasslands. Its wildlife includes the endangered lion-tailed macaque and Nilgiri tahr, as well as elephants, tigers, gaur, sambar and chital. The landscape supports more than 100 mammal species and 550 bird species. At a different ecological extreme, Himachal Pradesh’s Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve covers 7,770 square kilometres at elevations between 3,300 and 6,600 metres. Included in UNESCO’s network in 2025, it supports snow leopards, Himalayan ibex and blue sheep, alongside 732 vascular plant species, including 30 endemics. Around 12,000 people live in this demanding environment. Their livelihoods draw on pastoralism, yak and goat herding, barley and pea cultivation, and Tibetan herbal medicine. Off Tamil Nadu’s southeastern coast, the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve brings together coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangroves across approximately 10,500 square kilometres. These linked ecosystems support 4,223 plant and animal species. The reserve sustains around 25 lakh people across a region that includes approximately 47 coastal villages. The other Indian reserves recognised by UNESCO are Nanda Devi, Nokrek, Sundarbans, Great Nicobar, Similipal, Pachmarhi, Khangchendzonga, Agasthyamalai, Achanakmar-Amarkantak and Panna. Manas, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehang-Dibang, Great Rann of Kutch and Seshachalam complete India’s nationally notified network. national_raw_news.title: More than 21,000 devotees pay homage to sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang ...
national_raw_news.content: More than 21,000 devotees pay homage to sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang Monastery Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर More than 21,000 devotees pay homage to sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang Monastery ANI | Updated: Nov 06, 2026 11:38 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 6 (ANI): More than 21,000 devotees have visited Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) so far to offer prayers and pay homage to the sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha. According to a press release issued by the Ministry of Culture, devotees from Tawang and neighbouring regions of Arunachal Pradesh have been gathering at the monastery to seek blessings in the presence of the sacred relics. The exposition at Tawang Monastery will remain open to the public until November 7. The exposition holds special historical and spiritual significance as the sacred relics have returned to Arunachal Pradesh after a gap of 13 years, the release said. Brought from the National Museum, New Delhi, the relics offer Buddhist monks, nuns, devotees and the general public an opportunity to pay homage to the sacred remains of Shakyamuni Buddha and deepen their engagement with India's rich Buddhist heritage. The sacred relics were discovered at Piprahwah in Uttar Pradesh in 1898. Their discovery marked an important milestone in the archaeological history of Buddhism . Preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, the relics hold immense historical, archaeological and spiritual significance for Buddhist communities, the release noted. Two special exhibitions have also been organised at Tawang Monastery to highlight the rich legacy of Buddhism . ‘Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery’ by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) traces the discovery and historical significance of the relics. ‘Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives’, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, showcases the historical, artistic and cultural dimensions of Buddhism . Following the exposition at Tawang Monastery, the sacred relics will be taken to TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdilla, from November 8 to 13, 2026, and thereafter to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from November 14 to 20, 2026. The Holi relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on November 21, the release said. The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India in collaboration with the International Buddhist Confederation and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The initiative reflects the Government of India's commitment to preserving and promoting the country's rich Buddhist heritage and disseminating the timeless teachings of Bhagwan Buddha, centred on peace, compassion, wisdom and universal brotherhood. national_raw_news.content: India Successfully Tests Quasi-Ballistic Missile 'Pralay' Off Odisha Coast, Paving Way For Induction Into Armed Forces Defence India Successfully Tests Quasi-Ballistic Missile 'Pralay' Off Odisha Coast, Paving Way For Induction Into Armed Forces Swarajya Staff Nov 06, 2026 | Updated 08:20 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pralay Missile test (Pic Via PIB) India successfully flight-tested its indigenously developed Pralay quasi-ballistic missile off the Odisha coast on Thursday (5 November), marking a significant advancement towards operational induction into the armed forces. The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the test from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island as part of user evaluation trials. The missile met all stipulated objectives , with performance data captured and validated by various range instruments deployed by the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh described the trial as another significant milestone in strengthening India's indigenous defence capabilities. Research Centre Imarat in Hyderabad developed the missile in collaboration with other DRDO laboratories, whilst Bharat Dynamics Limited produced the system as one of the Development-cum-Production Partners. The successful test was conducted in the presence of senior DRDO officials, armed forces representatives and industry partners. Pralay is a solid-propellant surface-to-surface missile with a range of 150 to 500 kilometres and a payload capacity of 500 to 1,000 kilogrammes. The system employs state-of-the-art guidance and navigation technology, including an advanced Inertial Navigation System and Radio Frequency seeker to ensure high precision. The quasi-ballistic design enables the missile to follow a lower altitude trajectory with in-flight manoeuvres, making it significantly harder to intercept compared to traditional ballistic missiles. Defence Secretary and DRDO Chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh confirmed that the successful test brings the system's induction into the armed forces imminent, enhancing India's operational preparedness against emerging threats.
